rv.q: And it passed the ‘good date’ test with flying colours: this show made me feel very happy on the night, and on the morning after.
Tutty (Dear Evan Hansen) and Gift excel, and earn their standing ovation.
Dougal and Robin will surely be carrying that cake across New York for some time to come.
It’s that rare show in which you really take the characters to heart, and this contrasting pair are beautifully balanced on their parallel journeys to self-acceptance.
Two Strangers is as good a night out in the West End as you can get.
A warm and delightful production that proves that it’s possible to have one’s cake and eat it after all.
The endearing charm inherent in the characters adds oodles of oomph to a sweet show and the strongest reason to go see this well-deserved addition to the West End's current productions.
The score is fresh and tuneful, the lyrics witty and wise, and the sensational stars breathe real life into it all.

An incredible new British musical, Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) is uniquely special, it will melt your heart, and give you hope that your fortune can be changed by someone you’ve yet to meet.
Gift and Tutty share an electric chemistry on the West End stage and their comic friction is euphoric to watch.
This is a show where all elements are faultless, refreshingly tying together to make one clear and cohesive vision, flawlessly played out.
With a killer soundtrack, it is a must-see for theatregoers looking for a joyous and thoroughly entertaining experience.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this charming two-hander romcom as an intimate, heartfelt addition to the West End's recent wave of successful British musicals, praising its sweet tone, warm performances from Sam Tutty and Dujonna Gift, and quirky appeal.
